no: Let :g:`A_{1}B_{1}C_{1} << A_1 B_1 C_1 >>` be the 1st Morley triangle and (O) the circumcircle of ABC. Line AC_{1} cuts again (O) at A_{b} and B_{c}, C_{a} cyclically defined. Line AB_{1} cuts again (O) at A_{c} and B_{a}, C_{b} cyclically defined. Let \(S_{ab}\), \(S_{ac}\) be the Simson lines of A_{b} and A_{c}, resp, and denote \(S_{bc}\), \(S_{ba}\), \(S_{ca}\), \(S_{cb}\) cyclically. Let A_{bc} = \(S_{bc}\) ∩ \(S_{ca}\) and, cyclically, A_{ca} = \(S_{ca}\) ∩ \(S_{ab}\), A_{ab} = \(S_{ab}\) ∩ \(S_{bc}\). Let A_{cb} = \(S_{cb}\) ∩ \(S_{ba}\) and, cyclically, A_{ac} = \(S_{ac}\) ∩ \(S_{cb}\), A_{ba} = \(S_{ba}\) ∩ \(S_{ac}\).
A'B'C' is named here the **Hatzipolakis-Moses equilateral triangle**.
Note: Similar constructions can be done starting from the 2nd and 3rd Morley triangles, resulting in a 2nd- and 3rd-Hatzipolakis-Moses equilateral triangles.
